sources: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/inyo/recreation/camping-cabins (Inyo NF, read 2026-11-26), Dispersed Camping section: 'this camping is done anywhere on the forest outside of a developed campground. There are no services.'; 'Do not camp in the Restricted Recreation Area Boundary, typically where there are developed campgrounds and paved roadways.'; 'Stay on established roads, and do not drive off-road to camp.'; 'Select a campsite at least 200 feet from water.'; 'Obtain a California Fire Permit'; 'There are no bear boxes in dispersed camping areas.'; 'It is illegal to dump your black water on public lands'

https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/inyo/alerts (read 2026-11-26): no order naming Owens River Road or the Big Springs area

Esri World_Imagery 37.7370,-118.9677 (viewed 2026-11-26): pin on Owens River Road ~350 m east of US-395 in open Jeffrey pine forest, with dirt spurs and cleared pumice flats off both sides of the road

booking.source: Inyo NF camping page (dispersed camping anywhere outside developed campgrounds and the Recreation Restriction Areas) and Forest Order 05-04-50-25-17 (14 consecutive days within 10 miles of an undeveloped campsite; 28 days a year forest-wide), read 2026-11-26

note: Free dispersed camping on Inyo NF pull-offs and dirt spurs along Owens River Road east of US-395, near Big Springs between Mammoth Lakes and June Lake. No agency page names sites here: the forest allows dispersed camping outside its posted Recreation Restriction Areas, on established roads and at least 200 ft from water, with no services or bear boxes, and a California campfire permit for any stove or fire. Check the forest's restriction map and call the Mammoth Lakes Welcome Center before setting out. --Claude
summary: Owens River Road Dispersed (Inyo NF): no agency page designates sites; the Inyo camping page allows dispersed camping outside Recreation Restriction Areas. Kept as a free dispersed entry with a call-first caveat (AWH 2026-11-12 rule); 14-night limit from the forest order; imagery shows drive-in spurs and flats off the road. Phone confirmed.
flags: DESIGNATED SITES: none found - the Inyo NF publishes no page or list for Owens River Road dispersed sites; its camping page allows dispersed camping 'anywhere on the forest outside of a developed campground' except inside the Restricted Recreation Area Boundary ('typically where there are developed campgrounds and paved roadways'). The boundary map (Avenza / ESSRP 'Camp Like a Pro' app) could not be read, so whether the first, paved stretch of Owens River Road near the pin sits in a restriction area is UNREAD. Kept as a free dispersed site with a call-first caveat (AWH 2026-11-12); the reviewer may want the pin moved farther east along the road, past the paved section.
FIT: imagery shows dirt spurs and cleared pumice flats a 23-ft rig can reach off a paved road; the forest says to stay on established roads. No agency wording on rig size.
WEBSITE: the stored camping-cabins page is the Inyo's own dispersed-camping rules page - kept.
OHV: the area is near the Lookout Mountain OHV trails the forest mentions for Big Springs; this entry is general dispersed camping, not an OHV staging area. No action.
